front.title: Geneve network service interfaces option class

abstract.t: This specification defines a new Geneve Option Class and a registration procedure for corresponding option types that can be used for the exchange of metadata between network service domains. The metadata enables implementation of coordinated network service functionality across domains by carrying extra context.

section.name: Introduction
section.t: Following the publication of , IANA created a registry to manage the option class space. The option classes so far have been reserved for private use by different organizations from the “First come first served” range.

As enterprises evolve their network to span carriers, co-locations and public clouds, there is a desire to integrate with best-of-the- breed network and security services in a flexible and interoperable fashion. In many cases, these network service functionalities are offered as a managed service, which is usually hosted in a separate and independent network. This is a departure from the traditional model of enterprise network administrators managing service appliances within their premises.

Geneve is increasingly being adopted as the encapsulation protocol to tie these disparate networks together and offer coordinated services. At the point where a service needs to be applied to an enterprise’s traffic, network elements encapsulate the traffic over an on-demand Geneve overlay to a service endpoint while ensuring tenant isolation for the enterprise consuming the services. Geneve options carry extra context across domains to be used while applying the service.

This specification proposes a standard option class subrange under the “IETF review” range for such purposes, called “Network service interfaces Option Class”. It enables an “implement once and offer everywhere” approach that vendors and providers can leverage.

section.name: Options
section.t: This specification defines a new Option Class called “Network service interfaces Option Class" to carry extra context across domains that offer network services to enterprises. The new class will be structured as a subrange.

section.name: Origin Location
section.t: To serve localized content to end users, a network service may require the country of origin of the user traffic. This information is exchanged in a new option type called “origin location” that encodes the 10-bit country/subdivision code as standardized in ISO- 3166-2 [http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_3166]. section.name: IANA Considerations
section.t: IANA is requested to assign a new option class subrange from the “IETF Review” range to be called “Network service interfaces Option Class”. The suggested subrange is 0x0000 - 0x0009. IANA is also requested to maintain a new option type registry per option class in this subrange for "IETF expert review".

section.name: Security Considerations
section.t: There are no additional security risks introduced by this design.
